source.section: PDF page 12, Line 6 (federal AGI); PDF page 14, Line 11 NC Standard Deduction Chart, Line 14 and Line 15 (4.25%); PDF page 7, 'What is the Tax Rate?'; PDF page 14, Line 14 (negative NC taxable income is entered as negative) and Line 15 (zero tax when taxable income is zero or less)

worked: Federal AGI = wages 10,000.00. Federal taxable income = 10,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 0.00 (the federal figure is negative and is entered as zero) (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). D-400 Line 6 federal AGI 10,000.00. Line 7 additions (Schedule S Part A) 0.00. Line 8 = Line 6 + Line 7 = 10,000.00. Line 9 deductions (Schedule S Part B) 0.00. Line 10 child deduction 0.00 (no qualifying children). Line 11 NC standard deduction (single) 12,750.00. Line 12a = Lines 9 + 10 + 11 = 12,750.00; Line 12b = Line 8 - Line 12a = -2,750.00. Line 14 NC taxable income (full-year resident) = -2,750.00. Line 15: NC taxable income is zero or less, so the tax is 0.00. Line 16 credits 0.00; Line 17 income tax = 0.00. The form enters the negative amount on Line 14 with the negative circle filled; a consumer that floors taxable income at zero shows 0.00, with the same 0.00 tax. Floored at 0 for the expected value (checks brief rule 5a); the form's Line 14 shows -2750.00.
